course.title: Tiling
course.tagline: Lay floor and wall tiles straight, level and lasting.

days.title: Tiling Tools and Materials
days.goal: Know the tiling tools and materials.
steps: Lay out a tile cutter, notched trowel, spacers, level, sponge and bucket.
Learn the materials: tiles, adhesive (the glue), grout (the filler between tiles) and spacers.
A notched trowel is the flat tool with teeth that spreads adhesive evenly.
Set up a clean flat work area.
days.task: Label every tiling tool and material on your bench.
days.challenge: Name every tiling tool without looking.

quiz.q: What is tile adhesive?
options: The glue that sticks tiles to the floor or wall
quiz.explain: Adhesive is the glue that bonds tiles to the surface.

quiz.q: What is grout?
options: The paste that fills gaps between tiles
quiz.explain: Grout fills the joints between tiles and seals them.

quiz.q: What does a notched trowel do?
quiz.explain: The notches leave even ridges so tiles sit flat.

days.title: Plan a Tile Layout
days.goal: Plan where tiles go so cuts are even and the pattern is straight.
steps: Measure the floor and work out how many tiles you need.
Dry-lay tiles (lay them without glue) to check the pattern.
Plan so cut tiles at the edges are the same size both sides.
Mark the centre lines on the floor with chalk.
days.task: Draw a tile layout plan for a small floor.
days.challenge: Plan a floor so no cut tile is thinner than half a tile.

quiz.q: What should you work out before you lay any tiles?
options: The colour of the grout only.
quiz.explain: Measure the floor and work out how many tiles you need.

quiz.q: What is dry-laying?
options: Laying tiles without glue to check the pattern.
quiz.explain: Dry-lay tiles (lay them without glue) to check the pattern.

quiz.q: How should cut tiles at the edges look?
options: Big on one side and tiny on the other.
The same size on both sides.
quiz.explain: Plan so cut tiles at the edges are the same size both sides.

days.title: Prepare the Surface
days.goal: Get a floor or wall clean, flat and ready for tiles.
steps: Remove old tiles, glue and dust.
Fill holes and level dips with levelling compound.
Check the surface is flat with a long level.
Prime dusty surfaces so adhesive sticks.
days.task: Prepare a small floor area ready for tiling.
days.challenge: Check a floor is flat enough to tile.

quiz.q: What should you remove before you tile a surface?
quiz.explain: Remove old tiles, glue and dust.

quiz.q: What do you use to fill holes and level dips?
quiz.explain: Fill holes and level dips with levelling compound.

quiz.q: What should you do to a dusty surface so adhesive sticks?
quiz.explain: Prime dusty surfaces so adhesive sticks.

days.title: Cut Tiles Straight
days.goal: Cut tiles cleanly with a tile cutter.
steps: Mark the cut line on the tile with a pencil.
Score the tile once with the cutter wheel.
Snap the tile along the score line.
Smooth the cut edge with a rubbing stone.
days.task: Cut five tiles straight with no chips.
days.challenge: Cut a tile to an exact size first try.

quiz.q: What is the first step when you cut a tile?
options: Mark the cut line with a pencil.
quiz.explain: Mark the cut line on the tile with a pencil.

quiz.q: How do you score a tile with a cutter?
options: Score it once with the cutter wheel.
quiz.explain: Score the tile once with the cutter wheel.

quiz.q: What should you do to the cut edge after you snap the tile?
options: Smooth it with a rubbing stone.
quiz.explain: Smooth the cut edge with a rubbing stone.

days.title: Mix Adhesive
days.goal: Mix tile adhesive to the right thickness.
steps: Pour clean water in a bucket first, then add the powder.
Mix with a paddle until it is like thick peanut butter.
Let it rest for five minutes, then mix again.
Only mix as much as you can use in 30 minutes.
days.task: Mix a bucket of adhesive to the right thickness.
days.challenge: Mix adhesive that holds a ridge without slumping.

quiz.q: What goes in the bucket first when you mix adhesive?
quiz.explain: Pour clean water in a bucket first, then add the powder.

quiz.q: How thick should mixed adhesive be?
quiz.explain: Mix with a paddle until it is like thick peanut butter.

quiz.q: How much adhesive should you mix at once?
options: As much as the bucket holds.
Only as much as you can use in 30 minutes.
quiz.explain: Only mix as much as you can use in 30 minutes.

days.title: Spread Adhesive with a Notched Trowel
days.goal: Spread adhesive evenly so tiles stick flat.
steps: Scoop adhesive onto the floor with the flat side of the trowel.
Comb it with the notched side to make even ridges.
Hold the trowel at 45 degrees.
Spread only as much as you can tile in 15 minutes.
days.task: Spread adhesive in even ridges over one square metre.
days.challenge: Spread adhesive with ridges all the same height.

quiz.q: Which side of the trowel do you scoop adhesive with?
quiz.explain: Scoop adhesive onto the floor with the flat side of the trowel.

quiz.q: What angle should you hold the trowel at?
quiz.explain: Hold the trowel at 45 degrees.

quiz.q: How much adhesive should you spread at once?
options: Only as much as you can tile in 15 minutes.
quiz.explain: Spread only as much as you can tile in 15 minutes.

days.title: Project: Tile a Small Floor Area
days.goal: Tile a small floor area from layout to finished tiles.
steps: Dry-lay the tiles to check the pattern.
Spread adhesive and lay the tiles with spacers.
Check each tile is level with its neighbours.
Leave the tiles to set overnight before walking on them.
days.task: Finish a small tiled floor area, straight and level.
days.challenge: Lay tiles with no lips (edges sticking up) between them.

quiz.q: What should you do before you glue tiles in the project?
options: Dry-lay them to check the pattern.
quiz.explain: Dry-lay the tiles to check the pattern.

quiz.q: What keeps the gaps even as you lay the tiles?
quiz.explain: Spread adhesive and lay the tiles with spacers.

quiz.q: When can you walk on the new tiles?
quiz.explain: Leave the tiles to set overnight before walking on them.

project.title: Tile a Small Floor Area
project.brief: Tile a small floor area from layout to finished set tiles.

days.title: Tile Spacers and Straight Lines
days.goal: Use spacers to keep grout gaps even.
steps: Spacers are small plastic crosses that hold tiles apart.
Put spacers at every corner where tiles meet.
Check the lines stay straight with a long level.
Remove spacers before the adhesive sets hard.
days.task: Lay a row of tiles with perfectly even gaps.
days.challenge: Lay tiles so the grout lines are straight in both directions.

quiz.q: What are spacers?
options: Small plastic crosses that hold tiles apart.
quiz.explain: Spacers are small plastic crosses that hold tiles apart.

quiz.q: Where do you put spacers?
options: Only in the middle of the floor.
Put spacers at every corner where tiles meet.
quiz.explain: Put spacers at every corner where tiles meet.

quiz.q: When should you remove spacers?
quiz.explain: Remove spacers before the adhesive sets hard.

days.title: Check Tiles Are Level
days.goal: Check tiles as you lay them so the floor is flat.
steps: Press each tile down firmly and evenly.
Tap high tiles down gently with a rubber mallet.
Check with a level across two tiles at a time.
Lift and re-lay any tile that sits too high or low.
days.task: Lay six tiles perfectly level with each other.
days.challenge: Find and fix a tile that sits too high.

quiz.q: How should you press each tile down?
quiz.explain: Press each tile down firmly and evenly.

quiz.q: What should you do to a tile that sits too high?
options: Hit it hard with a hammer.
Tap it down gently with a rubber mallet.
quiz.explain: Tap high tiles down gently with a rubber mallet.

quiz.q: How do you check tiles are level?
options: With a level across two tiles at a time.
quiz.explain: Check with a level across two tiles at a time.

days.title: Lay Floor Tiles Step by Step
days.goal: Lay a full floor of tiles in the right order.
steps: Start from the centre lines and work outward.
Lay full tiles first, then cut the edge tiles.
Keep checking level and straight lines.
Clean adhesive off tile faces as you go.
days.task: Lay a full small floor of tiles.
days.challenge: Lay a floor with no adhesive left on the tile faces.

quiz.q: Where do you start laying floor tiles?
options: From the centre lines, working outward.
quiz.explain: Start from the centre lines and work outward.

quiz.q: Which tiles do you lay first?
options: Lay full tiles first, then cut the edge tiles.
quiz.explain: Lay full tiles first, then cut the edge tiles.

quiz.q: What should you clean off tile faces as you go?
quiz.explain: Clean adhesive off tile faces as you go.

days.title: Cut Tiles Around Pipes and Corners
days.goal: Cut tiles to fit around pipes, corners and door frames.
steps: Mark the pipe position on the tile.
Drill or nibble the hole with tile nippers.
Cut L-shapes for corners with two straight cuts.
Test the fit before you glue the tile down.
days.task: Cut a tile to fit around a pipe.
days.challenge: Cut an L-shaped tile that fits a corner exactly.

quiz.q: What should you do first when a tile must fit around a pipe?
options: Mark the pipe position on the tile.
quiz.explain: Mark the pipe position on the tile.

quiz.q: What tool makes the hole for a pipe?
options: Tile nippers to nibble the hole (or a drill).
quiz.explain: Drill or nibble the hole with tile nippers.

quiz.q: How do you cut an L-shape for a corner?
quiz.explain: Cut L-shapes for corners with two straight cuts.

days.title: Tile a Floor Like a Pro
days.goal: Finish a floor with neat edges and clean grout lines.
steps: Lay the last edge tiles and check they fit.
Clean all adhesive from the joints.
Leave the floor to set for 24 hours.
Walk on it gently and check nothing moves.
days.task: Finish a floor ready for grouting.
days.challenge: Lay a floor with even cuts at every edge.

quiz.q: What should you do with the last edge tiles?
options: Lay them and check they fit.
quiz.explain: Lay the last edge tiles and check they fit.

quiz.q: What should you clean from the joints before grouting?
quiz.explain: Clean all adhesive from the joints.

quiz.q: How long should the floor set before you walk on it?
quiz.explain: Leave the floor to set for 24 hours.

days.title: Tile a Bathroom Floor
days.goal: Tile a bathroom floor, working around the toilet and bath.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Floor

steps: Remove the toilet or work around its base.
Plan the layout so cuts are hidden under the bath.
Lay tiles with waterproof adhesive.
Seal the edges where tiles meet the bath and toilet.
days.task: Tile a bathroom floor area neatly.
days.challenge: Tile around a toilet base with neat cuts.

quiz.q: What should you do with the toilet before you tile a bathroom floor?
options: Remove it or work around its base.
quiz.explain: Remove the toilet or work around its base.

quiz.q: Where should you hide cut tiles in a bathroom?
options: In the middle of the floor.
quiz.explain: Plan the layout so cuts are hidden under the bath.

quiz.q: What kind of adhesive should you use in a bathroom?
quiz.explain: Lay tiles with waterproof adhesive.

days.title: Project: Tile a Bathroom Floor Section
days.goal: Tile a section of bathroom floor from prep to set tiles.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Floor

steps: Prepare the surface and plan the layout.
Lay the tiles with spacers and check level.
Cut tiles neatly around fittings.
Leave to set and clean the tile faces.
days.task: Finish a bathroom floor section, level and neat.
days.challenge: Tile the section with no lipped tiles.

quiz.q: What are tile spacers for?
options: Keeping grout gaps even between tiles
quiz.explain: Spacers hold tiles apart evenly so grout lines are straight.

quiz.q: What should you do after you lay the bathroom floor tiles?
options: Leave them to set and clean the tile faces.
quiz.explain: Leave to set and clean the tile faces.

quiz.q: How do you fix a tile that sits too high?
options: Lift it, add or remove adhesive, and re-lay it
quiz.explain: Lifting and re-laying is the only way to level a high tile.

project.title: Tile a Bathroom Floor Section
project.brief: Tile a section of bathroom floor, level and neat.

days.title: Tile a Bathroom Wall
days.goal: Tile a wall straight, starting from a level line.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Floor

steps: Mark a level starting line on the wall.
Fix a batten (a straight wooden strip) to support the first row.
Spread adhesive and lay tiles upward from the batten.
Use spacers and check level often.
days.task: Tile one wall section straight and level.
days.challenge: Tile a wall with no tiles slipping down.

quiz.q: What are tile spacers for?
options: Keeping grout gaps even between tiles
quiz.explain: Spacers hold tiles apart evenly so grout lines are straight.

quiz.q: What holds up the first row of wall tiles?
options: A batten, a straight wooden strip.
quiz.explain: Fix a batten (a straight wooden strip) to support the first row.

quiz.q: How do you fix a tile that sits too high?
options: Lift it, add or remove adhesive, and re-lay it
quiz.explain: Lifting and re-laying is the only way to level a high tile.

days.title: Tile Around a Shower
days.goal: Tile a shower area with waterproof prep.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Wall

steps: Learn that shower walls need a waterproof layer behind the tiles.
Use waterproof adhesive and grout.
Seal corners with silicone, not grout.
Check the tiles slope slightly toward the drain on the floor.
days.task: Tile a shower wall section with waterproof prep.
days.challenge: Seal a shower corner with neat silicone.

quiz.q: What must shower walls have behind the tiles?
quiz.explain: Shower walls need a waterproof layer behind the tiles.

quiz.q: What should you seal shower corners with?
quiz.explain: Seal corners with silicone, not grout.

quiz.q: How should a shower floor slope?
quiz.explain: Check the tiles slope slightly toward the drain on the floor.

days.title: Wall Tile Patterns
days.goal: Lay wall tiles in brick, straight and herringbone patterns.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Wall

steps: A brick pattern staggers each row by half a tile.
A straight pattern lines tiles up in a grid.
Herringbone lays tiles at 45 degrees in a zigzag.
Practise each pattern on a board.
days.task: Lay three patterns on a practice board.
days.challenge: Lay a brick pattern with even joints.

quiz.q: How does a brick pattern work?
options: Tiles line up in a grid.
Each row is staggered by half a tile.
Tiles lay at 45 degrees in a zigzag.
quiz.explain: A brick pattern staggers each row by half a tile.

quiz.q: How does a straight pattern work?
options: Each row is staggered by half a tile.
Tiles line up in a grid.
quiz.explain: A straight pattern lines tiles up in a grid.

quiz.q: How does a herringbone pattern work?
options: Tiles line up in a grid.
Tiles lay at 45 degrees in a zigzag.
quiz.explain: Herringbone lays tiles at 45 degrees in a zigzag.

days.title: Tile a Shower Wall
days.goal: Tile a full shower wall from prep to finish.

video.title: How to Tile a Bathroom Wall

steps: Check the waterproof layer is sound.
Plan the layout so cuts are at the edges.
Lay tiles from the bottom up with spacers.
Leave to set before grouting.
days.task: Finish a shower wall, straight and waterproof-ready.
days.challenge: Tile a shower wall with no hollow tiles.

quiz.q: What should you check before you tile a shower wall?
options: The colour of the grout only.
That the waterproof layer is sound.
quiz.explain: Check the waterproof layer is sound.

quiz.q: Where should cuts go on a shower wall layout?
quiz.explain: Plan the layout so cuts are at the edges.

quiz.q: Which way do you lay tiles on a shower wall?
options: From the bottom up, with spacers.
quiz.explain: Lay tiles from the bottom up with spacers.

days.title: Project: Tile a Bathroom Wall
days.goal: Tile a bathroom wall section from prep to set tiles.

video.title: How to Tile a Shower | Tile Prep and Installation

steps: Prepare the wall and mark level lines.
Lay tiles with spacers, checking level.
Cut tiles neatly around taps and fittings.
Clean the faces and leave to set.
days.task: Finish a bathroom wall section, straight and level.
days.challenge: Tile the wall with even grout lines.

quiz.q: What should you do to the wall first in the project?
options: Prepare it and mark level lines.
quiz.explain: Prepare the wall and mark level lines.

quiz.q: What should you cut tiles around on a bathroom wall?
quiz.explain: Cut tiles neatly around taps and fittings.

quiz.q: What should you do after you lay the wall tiles?
options: Clean the faces and leave them to set.
quiz.explain: Clean the faces and leave to set.

days.title: Grout Tiles
days.goal: Fill the gaps between tiles with grout.

video.title: How to Tile a Shower | Tile Prep and Installation

steps: Grout is the paste that fills the gaps between tiles.
Mix grout to a thick paste.
Push it into the joints with a grout float (a flat rubber tool).
Wipe the tiles clean with a damp sponge.
days.task: Grout a small tiled area cleanly.
days.challenge: Grout tiles with no grout haze left on the faces.

quiz.q: What is grout?
options: The paste that fills the gaps between tiles.
quiz.explain: Grout is the paste that fills the gaps between tiles.

quiz.q: How should you mix grout?
quiz.explain: Mix grout to a thick paste.

quiz.q: What tool pushes grout into the joints?
options: A grout float, a flat rubber tool.
quiz.explain: Push it into the joints with a grout float (a flat rubber tool).

days.title: Grout Colours and Sealing
days.goal: Pick grout colours and seal grout so it stays clean.

video.title: How to Tile a Shower | Tile Prep and Installation

steps: Pick a grout colour that suits the tiles.
Seal grout in wet areas so water cannot soak in.
Learn that white grout shows dirt; grey hides it.
Apply sealer with a small brush along the joints.
days.task: Seal the grout on a tiled area.
days.challenge: Pick a grout colour for a bathroom floor.

quiz.q: What should you think about when you pick a grout colour?
options: Pick a grout colour that suits the tiles.
quiz.explain: Pick a grout colour that suits the tiles.

quiz.q: Why seal grout in wet areas?
options: So water cannot soak into the grout.
quiz.explain: Seal grout in wet areas so water cannot soak in.

quiz.q: Which grout colour shows dirt more?
options: Grey shows dirt; white hides it.
White grout shows dirt; grey hides it.
quiz.explain: Learn that white grout shows dirt; grey hides it.

project.title: Tile a Bathroom Wall
project.brief: Tile a bathroom wall section from prep to set tiles.
checks: Wall prepared and level lines marked

days.title: Clean Grout Haze
days.goal: Remove the cloudy haze grout leaves on tiles.
steps: Wait until the grout is firm, then wipe with a damp sponge.
Change the rinse water often.
Buff the tiles with a dry cloth.
Use a haze remover for stubborn cloudiness.
days.task: Clean a grouted area until the tiles shine.
days.challenge: Remove haze without scratching the tiles.

quiz.q: When should you wipe the grout haze off the tiles?
options: When the grout is firm, with a damp sponge.
Right away while the grout is wet.
quiz.explain: Wait until the grout is firm, then wipe with a damp sponge.

quiz.q: Why wipe tiles with a damp sponge after grouting?
options: To remove grout from the tile faces before it hardens
quiz.explain: Grout left on faces hardens into a haze that is hard to remove.

quiz.q: What is grout haze?
options: The cloudy film grout leaves on tile faces
quiz.explain: Haze is the thin cloudy film left if grout is not wiped off.

days.title: Fix a Loose Tile
days.goal: Find and fix a loose or hollow tile.
steps: Tap tiles: a hollow sound means the adhesive failed.
Lift the loose tile carefully.
Clean off old adhesive and re-stick it.
Grout the joints again and leave to set.
days.task: Fix a loose tile so it sounds solid.
days.challenge: Find a hollow tile by tapping.

quiz.q: How do you find a loose tile?
options: Tap it: a hollow sound means the adhesive failed.
quiz.explain: Tap tiles: a hollow sound means the adhesive failed.

quiz.q: What should you do after you lift a loose tile?
options: Clean off old adhesive and re-stick it.
quiz.explain: Clean off old adhesive and re-stick it.

quiz.q: What should you do after you re-stick the tile?
options: Grout the joints again and leave it to set.
quiz.explain: Grout the joints again and leave to set.

days.title: Silicone Seals
days.goal: Seal edges with silicone for a waterproof finish.
steps: Cut the silicone tube nozzle at an angle.
Apply a smooth bead along the joint.
Smooth it with a wet finger in one pass.
Let it dry fully before using the shower.
days.task: Seal a bath edge with neat silicone.
days.challenge: Apply silicone in one smooth bead with no gaps.

quiz.q: How should you cut a silicone tube nozzle?
quiz.explain: Cut the silicone tube nozzle at an angle.

quiz.q: How do you smooth a silicone bead?
options: With a wet finger in one pass.
quiz.explain: Smooth it with a wet finger in one pass.

quiz.q: When can you use the shower after sealing?
quiz.explain: Let it dry fully before using the shower.

days.title: Bonding Ceramic Tiles
days.goal: Know how ceramic tiles bond to different surfaces.
steps: Ceramic tiles need the right adhesive for the surface.
Learn that wood, concrete and plaster need different prep.
Use flexible adhesive on floors that move slightly.
Test a tile bond by trying to lift it after setting.
days.task: Bond tiles to two different surfaces and test them.
days.challenge: Pick the right adhesive for a wooden floor.

quiz.q: What do ceramic tiles need for different surfaces?
options: The right adhesive for the surface.
quiz.explain: Ceramic tiles need the right adhesive for the surface.

quiz.q: Which surfaces need different prep?
quiz.explain: Learn that wood, concrete and plaster need different prep.

quiz.q: What kind of adhesive should you use on floors that move slightly?
quiz.explain: Use flexible adhesive on floors that move slightly.

days.title: Price a Tiling Job
days.goal: Price a tiling job from tiles, adhesive, time and profit.
steps: Measure the area and work out tiles needed, plus 10 percent spare.
Add adhesive, grout and spacers to the cost.
Time the job and value your hours fairly.
Write a simple quote a customer can understand.
days.task: Write a clear quote for tiling a bathroom floor.
days.challenge: Price a kitchen wall job fairly.

quiz.q: How many spare tiles should you buy for a job?
quiz.explain: Measure the area and work out tiles needed, plus 10 percent spare.

quiz.q: What should you add to the tile cost in a quote?
quiz.explain: Add adhesive, grout and spacers to the cost.

quiz.q: What should a tiling quote include?
options: Tiles, adhesive, grout, time and profit
quiz.explain: A real quote covers materials, time and profit.

days.title: Grout a Floor Like a Pro
days.goal: Grout a tiled floor cleanly with even joints.
steps: Mix grout to a thick paste, like peanut butter.
Push grout into the joints with a rubber float.
Wipe the tiles with a damp sponge at an angle.
Let it dry, then buff off the haze with a dry cloth.
days.task: Grout a small floor area with even joints.
days.challenge: Grout a floor with no haze left on the tiles.

quiz.q: How thick should you mix grout for a floor?
quiz.explain: Mix grout to a thick paste, like peanut butter.

quiz.q: How should you wipe the tiles after grouting?
options: With a damp sponge at an angle.
quiz.explain: Wipe the tiles with a damp sponge at an angle.

quiz.q: What should you do after the grout dries?
options: Buff off the haze with a dry cloth.
quiz.explain: Let it dry, then buff off the haze with a dry cloth.

days.title: Bond Ceramic Tiles to a Wall
days.goal: Stick ceramic tiles to a wall with the right adhesive.
steps: Choose adhesive made for ceramic tiles.
Spread it with a notched trowel.
Press each tile firmly and check it is level.
Leave the tiles to set before you grout.
days.task: Bond ceramic tiles to a wall section.
days.challenge: Stick tiles that stay put and level.

quiz.q: What holds ceramic tiles to a wall?
options: Tile adhesive spread with a notched trowel
quiz.explain: Tile adhesive bonds tiles to the wall; the notched trowel spreads it evenly.

quiz.q: Why press each tile firmly?
options: So the adhesive grips the tile fully
quiz.explain: Firm pressure pushes the tile into the adhesive so it bonds well.

quiz.q: When can you grout a tiled wall?
options: After the adhesive has set fully
quiz.explain: Grouting before the adhesive sets can move the tiles out of place.

days.title: Capstone Planning
days.goal: Choose your capstone tiling job, buy tiles and plan the days.
steps: Pick a real floor or wall that needs tiling.
Choose tiles with the owner and buy them plus 10 percent spare.
Plan the layout on paper first.
Write a two-day plan with setting and grouting time.
days.task: Have all capstone tiles bought and the layout planned.
days.challenge: Plan a capstone job that uses floor or wall tiling plus grout.

quiz.q: What should you pick first for your capstone?
options: A real floor or wall that needs tiling.
quiz.explain: Pick a real floor or wall that needs tiling.

quiz.q: What should you plan on paper first for the capstone?
quiz.explain: Plan the layout on paper first.

quiz.q: What should you write before you start the capstone?
options: A two-day plan with setting and grouting time.
quiz.explain: Write a two-day plan with setting and grouting time.

days.title: Capstone: Tile a Real Floor or Wall
days.goal: Tile a real floor or wall, grout it and present it.
steps: Prepare, lay and grout following your plan.
Check level and straight lines as you work.
Clean up fully and show the owner the result.
Present your quote, tiles used and care notes.
days.task: Present a finished tiled floor or wall with photos and quote.
days.challenge: Finish with time left for a final clean and check.

quiz.q: What should you do as you tile the capstone job?
options: Work as fast as possible with no checks.
Check level and straight lines as you work.
quiz.explain: Check level and straight lines as you work.

quiz.q: What should you do when the capstone tiling is done?
options: Clean up fully and show the owner the result.
quiz.explain: Clean up fully and show the owner the result.

quiz.q: What should you present with the finished job?
options: Your quote, tiles used and care notes.
quiz.explain: Present your quote, tiles used and care notes.

capstone.title: Tile a Real Floor or Wall
capstone.brief: Tile a real floor or wall, grout it and seal it, and present it with the quote and tiles used.
checks: Tiles straight, level and firmly stuck
Grout even and clean with no haze
Edges sealed with silicone where needed
Area clean and tidy on handover
Quote, tiles and care notes presented
deliverables: Quote with tiles, materials, time and price
List of tiles and materials used
